concepts.name: Formation and Ideological Basis of the All India Forward Bloc (1939)
key_dimensions: Circumstances leading to formation: post-Tripuri Congress crisis and Bose's resignation from Congress presidency
Ideological positioning: left-wing nationalism distinct from both Gandhian Congress and the Communist Party of India
Initial composition: merger of left factions within Congress vs. independent party status
UPSC trap: Forward Bloc was formed within Congress first (May 1939) before becoming a separate party — the distinction between 'faction' and 'party' phases

concepts.name: Subhas Chandra Bose's Elections as Congress President: Haripura (1938) and Tripuri (1939)
key_dimensions: Haripura Session (1938): unanimous election, Presidential address themes — industrialization, planned economy, anti-imperialism
Tripuri Session (1939): contested election against Pattabhi Sitaramayya (Gandhi's candidate), Bose wins — significance of this defiance
Gandhi's statement 'Pattabhi's defeat is my defeat' and its political implications
UPSC trap: confusing which session was contested vs. unanimous; Tripuri is the controversial one

concepts.name: Bose's Resignation from Congress Presidency and the Working Committee Crisis (1939)
key_dimensions: Reasons for resignation: inability to form Working Committee of his choice, non-cooperation by senior Congress leaders
Role of Gandhi and right-wing Congress leadership in isolating Bose
Constitutional dimensions: Bose's argument about democratic mandate vs. organizational discipline
Consequences: his marginalization within Congress and the path to Forward Bloc formation

concepts.name: Bose's Ideological Framework: Synthesis of Nationalism, Socialism, and Authoritarianism
key_dimensions: Admiration for Soviet planning model and fascist organizational efficiency — the controversial synthesis
Rejection of Gandhian non-violence as the sole method of achieving independence
His book 'The Indian Struggle' (1935): analysis of Indian nationalism and critique of Congress strategy
UPSC trap: Bose's admiration for certain fascist organizational methods ≠ ideological fascist; distinction is critical

concepts.name: Bose's Escape from India (1941) and the 'Great Escape' Narrative
key_dimensions: Context: house arrest under Regulation III of 1818 after his anti-war activism
Route of escape: Calcutta → Peshawar → Kabul → Moscow → Berlin (via Afghanistan in disguise as Ziauddin)
Political significance: demonstrated rejection of passive resistance and commitment to armed struggle
UPSC trap: the escape was to Germany first, NOT directly to Southeast Asia — common confusion with later INA phase

concepts.name: Bose in Germany: The Free India Centre and Indian Legion (1941–1943)
key_dimensions: Establishment of Free India Centre (Azad Hind) in Berlin and radio propaganda via Azad Hind Radio
Formation of Indian Legion (Indische Legion) from Indian POWs captured in North Africa
Nature of German support: strategic/instrumental vs. genuine anti-colonial sympathy — Hitler's racial hierarchy problem
UPSC trap: Indian Legion fought under German command in Europe, NOT the INA which fought in Southeast Asia — two different armed formations

concepts.name: Transfer from Germany to Southeast Asia: The Submarine Journey (1943)
key_dimensions: Reason for shift: German campaign stalling, Japanese advances in Asia offered better opportunity
Historic submarine transfer: German U-boat to Japanese submarine near Madagascar — only such transfer in WWII
Strategic logic: proximity to India via Burma front made Southeast Asian theatre more viable
Significance: demonstrates Bose's pragmatic geopolitical thinking over ideological loyalty to any Axis power

concepts.name: Indian National Army (INA) / Azad Hind Fauj: Origins and Reorganization under Bose
key_dimensions: Original INA: formed by Mohan Singh (1942) from Indian POWs after fall of Singapore — Bose was NOT its founder
Dissolution of first INA and its reconstitution under Bose after he arrived in Singapore (1943)
Composition: Indian POWs + Indian civilian diaspora in Southeast Asia (Malaya, Burma, Singapore)
UPSC trap: Bose did not found the INA — he reorganized and led it; Mohan Singh was the original founder

concepts.name: Azad Hind Government (Provisional Government of Free India, 1943)
key_dimensions: Declared on October 21, 1943 in Singapore — first 'government' of free India in exile
Recognition received from Axis powers and their allies (Japan, Germany, Italy, Burma, Thailand, etc.) — NOT Allied powers
Symbolic declaration of war against Britain and USA
UPSC trap: this government had no territory initially; it received the Andaman & Nicobar Islands (renamed Shahid and Swaraj Dweep) under nominal Japanese transfer

concepts.name: INA Military Campaigns: Imphal and Kohima (1944) — 'Chalo Delhi' March
key_dimensions: 'Chalo Delhi' (March to Delhi) as the battle cry and its psychological-political significance
INA's role in the Imphal-Kohima campaign alongside Japanese forces — initial advances and eventual retreat
Reasons for failure: Allied air superiority, supply line collapse, monsoon, Japanese strategic withdrawal
UPSC trap: INA came closest to Indian soil at Moirang (Manipur) where the tricolor was hoisted — NOT Delhi

concepts.name: Rani of Jhansi Regiment: Women's Wing of INA
key_dimensions: First organized armed women's regiment in Indian nationalist movement — formed under Lakshmi Sahgal
Roles: primarily nursing and support, but also trained for combat — significance for women's participation in armed nationalism
Contrast with other nationalist movements' approach to women's participation
UPSC angle: Lakshmi Sahgal's later life and the INA trials connection — she was also tried

concepts.name: Death of Subhas Chandra Bose (August 1945) — Controversy and Theories
key_dimensions: Official account: died in a plane crash in Taihoku (Taipei), Taiwan on August 18, 1945
Competing theories: Stalin theory (captured by Soviets), survival theories, various commission investigations
Official Indian government investigations: Shah Nawaz Committee (1956), Khosla Commission (1974), Mukherjee Commission (1999–2005)
UPSC trap: Mukherjee Commission concluded he did NOT die in the plane crash — but Government of India REJECTED this finding; official position remains the plane crash

concepts.name: INA Trials (Red Fort Trials, 1945–46) and Their Political Backfire
key_dimensions: Three prominent accused: Shah Nawaz Khan (Muslim), Gurbaksh Singh Dhillon (Sikh), Prem Kumar Sahgal (Hindu) — deliberate symbolic selection
Defense team: Bhulabhai Desai (lead), Jawaharlal Nehru, Tej Bahadur Sapru — Congress's strategic embrace of INA cause
Political consequence: trials became a massive propaganda disaster for British; united Indian public opinion, triggered Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (1946)
UPSC trap: all three main accused were eventually released (not acquitted) due to political pressure — distinction between acquittal and release matters

concepts.name: Royal Indian Navy Mutiny (1946) and the INA Effect
key_dimensions: Direct trigger: INA trials and the British handling of Indian servicemen who fought for independence
Spread from HMIS Talwar (Bombay) to multiple ships and naval establishments across India
Congress and Muslim League's ambivalent response: initial support then urging surrender — why leaders were cautious about armed uprising
Significance: demonstrated that British could no longer rely on Indian armed forces — accelerated transfer of power decision

concepts.name: Bose's Relationship with Gandhi and Nehru: Ideological and Personal Tensions
key_dimensions: Bose vs. Gandhi: fundamental disagreement on non-violence, pace of independence, and mass mobilization vs. negotiation
Bose vs. Nehru: both leftist but Nehru remained within Congress discipline; Nehru's criticism of Bose's Axis alliance
Personal correspondence and mutual respect alongside political opposition — nuanced relationship
UPSC angle: Gandhi calling Bose 'Patriots of patriots' / 'Netaji' vs. opposing him politically — apparent contradiction

concepts.name: Bose's Economic Vision: Planned Industrialization and the National Planning Committee (1938)
key_dimensions: Bose as Congress President established the National Planning Committee (1938) under Jawaharlal Nehru's chairmanship
Vision for rapid industrialization modeled on Soviet Five-Year Plans — influence on post-independence planning
Tension between his economic modernism and Gandhi's village/cottage industry model
UPSC trap: NPC was established by Bose but chaired by Nehru — the founding vs. leading distinction

concepts.name: Forward Bloc's Stance on World War II and the 'Enemy's Enemy' Strategic Logic
key_dimensions: Bose's position: Britain's war crisis is India's opportunity — directly opposite to Congress's conditional support
Contrast with Congress: 'Quit India' (1942) vs. Bose's active military alliance with Axis powers
Contrast with Communist Party of India: CPI supported Allied war effort after Germany attacked USSR (1941) — 'People's War' thesis
UPSC trap: three distinct responses to WWII — Congress (Quit India/non-cooperation), CPI (support Allied war), Forward Bloc/Bose (ally with Axis against Britain)

concepts.name: Legacy and Posthumous Rehabilitation of Bose and INA in Indian National Memory
key_dimensions: Initial post-independence ambivalence: Nehru government's reluctance to fully rehabilitate INA soldiers (pension, rank recognition issues)
Gradual elevation to national hero status: Netaji as honorific, his portrait in Parliament's Central Hall
Declassification of Netaji files (2015–2016) by Modi government — political dimensions of historical memory
UPSC contemporary angle: renaming of Andaman's Ross Island as 'Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose Island' (2018) and India Gate canopy statue (2022)

concepts.name: Bose's Concept of 'Samyavad' and Critique of Both Capitalism and Orthodox Communism
key_dimensions: Samyavad: Bose's term for an Indian form of socialism distinct from Soviet communism and Western capitalism
Emphasis on national unity transcending class struggle — contrast with Marxist class-conflict framework
Influence of Indian philosophical traditions on his political thought alongside Western socialist ideas
UPSC angle: how this distinguishes him from M.N. Roy (orthodox communist) and Gandhi (trusteeship model) — a three-way ideological comparison

concepts.name: Singapore as the Nerve Centre of INA: Cathay Building and the Symbolic Geography of Azad Hind
key_dimensions: Singapore's fall (February 1942) as the turning point that made INA possible — largest surrender of British-led forces
INA Headquarters at Cathay Building, Singapore; Bose's residence and operational command
The INA Memorial (later demolished by British) and its significance in collective memory
UPSC angle: the Indian diaspora in Malaya/Singapore as financial and human resource backbone of INA — civilian vs. POW contributions
